author: reek
body: A signature is 64 bytes and the length field must say so.

author: reek
body: 1 context byte + 3 list-length bytes + 3 cert-length bytes + the DER + 2 extension bytes.

author: reek
body: THIS NOW READS THE EXTENSION THAT GOES ON THE WIRE. It used to read TlsCert's tls-sigalgs-ext, a second hand-written copy that no ClientHello ever contained: the real one is Tls's tls-ext-sig-algs, built by tls-build-extensions. So this section asserted the contents of a constant no server could see, and would have gone on passing while the extension actually sent said something else. The decorative copy is deleted.

author: reek
body: Type 13, then the extension length, then the list length, then the schemes. Each scheme is two bytes, and the three headers above them are two bytes each, so N schemes is 2N + 6 bytes in all.

author: reek
body: Every scheme offered must be one tls-cv-verify will actually accept. That is the property worth asserting: the two sets are written down in two places -- the extension here, the dispatch in TlsCert -- and nothing but this line makes them agree.
